subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` archive convention and physical purge behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration/purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: Source inspection proves current main still has the reported naming and deletion behavior, but changing shipped filenames, cleanup semantics, disk-budget behavior, and downstream-tool expectations is a storage/product contract decision rather than a safe autonomous bug fix.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, migrate/backfill old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts through doctor or a storage migration, and keep physical purge only behind an explicit documented retention contract.

options.title: Keep current behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave suffixes and retention cleanup unchanged, and document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk budget physically removes it.

options.title: Split no-delete from naming cleanup
options.body: Use the terminology/config issue for naming and prune semantics while separately deciding whether any OpenClaw-owned transcript artifact may ever be physically purged.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, migrate/backfill old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts through doctor or a storage migration, and keep physical purge only behind an explicit documented retention contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session lifecycle work and current-line blame make this the best available owner for choosing the user-facing storage lifecycle contract.
